faq.metaDescription: Answers on cost, duration, what we need to start, what cannot be recovered, and how Revault keeps your case confidential.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: The questions we get before people decide to reach out.

needToStart.q: What do you need from me to start?
needToStart.a: Only your story: the type of wallet, what happened and what you still have — a wallet file, a backup, part of a seed phrase or the old device. Never share seed phrases, private keys or passwords at this stage.

cost.q: How much does a recovery cost?
cost.a: We work no cure, no pay. The standard fee is a percentage of the recovered value, agreed and contracted before we start, and only due after access is restored. High-value wallets get a custom rate.

duration.a: It depends on the case. Simple password cases can finish within days; complex passwords or partial seed phrases can take weeks or occasionally months. You get a realistic estimate after the intake.

trust.q: How can I trust you with my wallet?
trust.a: Both parties sign a service agreement under Dutch law before any work. You keep control of the wallet and the funds at all times: we rebuild access, you open the wallet and move the funds yourself.

chances.q: What are the chances of success?
chances.a: It depends entirely on what you still have. A forgotten password with partial memory, or a seed phrase missing a few words, is often recoverable. We assess honestly before you commit.

littleInfo.q: Can you help if I have very little information?
littleInfo.a: Sometimes. Limited information narrows the options but doesn't automatically rule recovery out. We'll ask a few questions and tell you upfront if we don't think we can help.

currencies.a: Recovery happens at the wallet level, so the currency rarely matters — Bitcoin, Ethereum and tokens, Litecoin, Dogecoin, XRP and most others. The wallet type and available material determine viability.

wrongAddress.q: Can you reverse a transaction sent to the wrong address?
wrongAddress.a: No. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. If you sent funds to an exchange on the wrong network or without a tag, that exchange's support is your route.

stolen.q: Can you recover stolen crypto or scam losses?
stolen.a: No. We don't take stolen-fund or scam cases, and we don't trace transactions. Any service claiming it can reverse a blockchain transaction is describing something that cannot be done.

lostSeed.q: My seed phrase is completely gone. Can you help?
lostSeed.a: Not if no other wallet material exists — no file, no key, no backup, no device. Nobody can recover that, including us.

inheritance.q: Do you help with inherited wallets?
inheritance.a: Yes. We work with heirs, executors, notaries and lawyers. Every inheritance case starts with verification of identity, authority and ownership before any technical work.

location.q: Do I have to come to you?
location.a: No. Sessions can be fully remote over a secured connection, at our office, at your premises or at a notary's office. Your adviser is welcome to attend.

password-recovery.name: Password recovery
password-recovery.short: Forgotten wallet passwords, extra passphrases and encrypted backup files.
password-recovery.intro: You remember some of it — a pattern, a few words, a year — but not enough. We turn what you remember into a targeted search on isolated systems.
password-recovery.metaDescription: Forgotten your crypto wallet password or passphrase? Revault runs targeted, offline recovery from what you still remember. No recovery, no fee.

can.one: Encrypted wallet files (wallet.dat, keystore, Electrum, Ledger/Trezor passphrase)
can.two: The optional 25th-word passphrase alongside a seed phrase
can.three: Password-protected archives and backup files holding wallet data

need.one: The wallet file or device (shared only after the agreement)
need.two: Everything you remember about the password: fragments, habits, other passwords from that era
need.three: Evidence that the wallet is yours

one.q: What if I remember nothing at all?
one.a: A search with no clues is rarely realistic. We'll tell you that at the intake instead of taking the case.

two.q: Do you keep my wallet file?
two.a: No. Material is handled under the agreement, in an isolated environment, and deleted after handover.

seed-phrase-reconstruction.name: Seed phrase reconstruction
seed-phrase-reconstruction.short: Missing, wrong or swapped words in a 12- or 24-word recovery phrase.
seed-phrase-reconstruction.intro: A seed phrase with a few missing or misspelled words, in the wrong order, or that fails validation can often be reconstructed — provided enough of it survives.
seed-phrase-reconstruction.metaDescription: Seed phrase with missing, wrong or swapped words? Revault reconstructs incomplete recovery phrases on air-gapped systems. No recovery, no fee.

can.one: A few missing or misspelled words
can.two: Words in the wrong order or an unknown derivation path
can.three: Damaged paper or metal backups, with document-restoration partners if needed

need.one: The surviving words and their positions, shared only after the agreement
need.two: The wallet software or device that generated the phrase
need.three: A known address or transaction to confirm the result

one.q: How many missing words is too many?
one.a: It depends on the phrase length and what else is known. We calculate the search space before accepting the case.

two.a: Then reconstruction is not possible for anyone. We only take cases where meaningful material remains.

damaged-wallet.name: Damaged wallet files
damaged-wallet.short: Corrupted wallet.dat, broken keystores and unreadable backups.
damaged-wallet.intro: A wallet file that refuses to open is not necessarily lost. We analyse the file's structure and rebuild what's recoverable in a compatible environment.
damaged-wallet.metaDescription: Corrupted or damaged wallet file? Revault analyses and repairs broken wallet.dat, keystore and backup files. No recovery, no fee.

can.three: Wallet data on failing drives, with data-recovery partners where needed

need.two: The software and version that created it

one.q: Can you recover a deleted wallet file?
one.a: Sometimes, if the drive hasn't been heavily used since. Stop using the device and contact us.

two.q: Do you need the drive physically?
two.a: For physical damage, yes. For file-level corruption a remote session is usually enough.

legacy-wallet.name: Legacy wallet recovery
legacy-wallet.short: Discontinued or unsupported wallet software from the early years.
legacy-wallet.intro: MultiBit, Jaxx, old Blockchain.info backups, early Bitcoin Core: software that no longer runs on a modern machine. We rebuild a compatible environment and extract the keys.
legacy-wallet.metaDescription: Old wallet from discontinued software that no longer opens? Revault rebuilds compatible environments for MultiBit, Jaxx, early Bitcoin Core and more.

can.one: Discontinued wallets (MultiBit, Jaxx, Armory, early mobile wallets)
can.two: Old backup formats and encrypted export files
can.three: Migration to a modern wallet you control

need.one: The wallet file, backup or device
need.two: What you remember about the software and its version

one.q: The company behind my wallet no longer exists.
one.a: That's common and usually not a blocker. Most legacy formats are documented or reverse-engineered.

two.q: Will you move my coins for me?
two.a: No. We restore access; you move the funds to a new wallet yourself, with us present if you want.

hardware-wallet.name: Hardware wallet recovery
hardware-wallet.short: Broken screens, dead USB ports and forgotten PINs on Ledger and Trezor.
hardware-wallet.intro: The coins were never on the device — they're on the blockchain. Whether the device is broken or the PIN is gone, access can usually be rebuilt from the recovery phrase or the device itself.
hardware-wallet.metaDescription: Broken or locked Ledger or Trezor? Revault restores access from a damaged device or an incomplete recovery phrase. Non-custodial. No recovery, no fee.

can.one: Physical defects: cracked screens, dead ports, water damage
can.three: Incomplete recovery phrases from the device's original setup

one.a: We don't attack the device's secure element. Recovery comes from the recovery phrase, passphrase knowledge or hardware repair.

two.q: My device is from a discontinued brand.
two.a: Most hardware wallets follow the same BIP standards; the phrase usually works in another wallet.

about.metaDescription: Revault is a Dutch, non-custodial crypto wallet recovery specialist built on honest assessments, contract-first work and never holding client funds.
about.title: Recovery without the shady part.
about.subtitle: Crypto recovery has a reputation problem. Revault exists to be the version that a notary would be comfortable recommending.

story.one: Most people who lose access to a wallet did nothing wrong. They chose a strong password in 2014, wrote a seed phrase on paper that got damp, or inherited a laptop from a parent who never explained what was on it.
story.two: The industry that grew up around those people is split between serious engineers and outright scammers, and from the outside they look the same. We built Revault around the things that make the difference visible: a contract before work, verification before a case is accepted, air-gapped systems, and a fee that only exists when access is restored.
story.three: We say no to cases we can't win. A completely lost seed phrase, stolen funds, a transaction to the wrong address — we'll tell you that in the first conversation rather than let you hope.

honesty.title: Honest first
honesty.body: A realistic assessment before you commit, including when the answer is no.

security.title: Security by design
security.body: Isolated systems, no cloud, no secrets over email, and an NDA when you want one.

control.title: You stay in control
control.body: We never hold funds. You open the wallet and move the assets yourself.

privacy.metaDescription: How Revault handles personal data submitted through this website and during a recovery case.
privacy.title: Privacy policy

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Through the intake form: your name, email, optional phone number, and the description of your case. During a case: identity documents required for KYC/AML verification and the technical material needed for recovery, handled under the service agreement.

sections.title: What we never ask for online
sections.body: Seed phrases, private keys and passwords. Any material of that kind is only handled after a signed agreement, in an isolated environment, and is deleted after handover.

sections.title: How we use it
sections.body: To assess and, if agreed, execute your case; to comply with legal obligations; and for anonymous page-view statistics without cookies or third-party trackers.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Intake requests that don't become a case are deleted after 12 months. Case files are retained as required by Dutch law for identification and tax purposes, then deleted.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can request access, correction or deletion of your personal data by emailing us. We respond within 30 days.

terms.metaDescription: The general terms under which Revault provides wallet recovery services.
terms.title: Terms & conditions

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: Revault provides non-custodial technical services to restore access to cryptocurrency wallets owned by, or legally under the authority of, the client. Revault does not recover stolen funds, trace transactions or investigate fraud.

sections.title: Assessment
sections.body: The initial assessment is free and non-binding. It is an estimate of technical feasibility, not a guarantee of success.

sections.title: Agreement
sections.body: No recovery work starts before a written service agreement is signed by both parties covering scope, fee, confidentiality and security arrangements. An NDA is available on request.

sections.title: Fee
sections.body: The fee is a percentage of the recovered value agreed in the service agreement, due only after access has been successfully restored. No fee is due if recovery fails.

sections.title: Non-custodial
sections.body: Revault never takes custody of client assets. After a successful recovery the client opens the wallet and transfers the assets to a wallet under their own control.

sections.title: Governing law
sections.body: These terms and every service agreement are governed by Dutch law. Disputes are submitted to the competent court in the Netherlands.
